why: Nested calls on one CPU form a call stack: the function on top is the one running. Each log event charges the elapsed time to the current top, then pushes or pops. It is matching start/end pairs where the stack also tells you who owns the time between events.
hints: Between two consecutive log records, which function is running?
The innermost unfinished call: the top of a stack of function IDs. A start pauses it, an end resumes the one below.
Keep prev = first uncharged second. On start at t: charge t - prev to the top (if any), push, prev = t. On end at t: charge t - prev + 1 to the popped ID, prev = t + 1.
pitfalls: An end timestamp is inclusive (that second counts), so the next second starts at t + 1.
Recursive calls of the same ID are separate stack entries; their times add up in the same total.
Idle time between top-level calls belongs to no function.
